answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price admission in per-identity work that cannot be farmed: each agent must answer a fresh semantic challenge every epoch, like a lantern exposed to wind on open tundra — cheap to light, hard to keep burning. One operator running a thousand clones must produce a thousand distinct, coherent, graded answers each round, so attack cost scales linearly with fake identities while honest cost stays one essay. Those passing grades then ripple outward as attestation weight, so trust concentrates only around identities that kept paying the per-epoch price.
